title: Winlogon Shell or Userinit value hijack
description: Detects a Winlogon Shell or Userinit registry value set to a non-default executable command.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may replace or extend the Winlogon Shell or Userinit command to execute code during interactive logon.
hypothesis.rationale: MITRE documents Winlogon helper modification as a persistence and privilege-escalation mechanism. Selecting only Shell or Userinit under the exact Winlogon key and excluding their standard Windows values is more precise than monitoring the complete key.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify non-default executable content written to Winlogon Shell or Userinit while leaving standard values, unrelated registry locations and non-set actions unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint registry events

triage.summary: Treat a non-default Winlogon command as a high-priority persistence signal and determine whether a documented shell, kiosk or virtual-desktop configuration explains it.
steps: Review the complete value data, registry hive, writer process, writer command, account and endpoint role.
Inspect every referenced executable or script and correlate its creation, signer, hash, parent process and execution around interactive logons.
Confirm an approved custom shell or VDI configuration with its owner; otherwise contain the endpoint, restore the trusted value and investigate credential or privilege abuse.
false_positives: Approved kiosk, virtual-desktop, embedded-system or custom-shell configurations that intentionally replace the standard Winlogon command

validation.expected_outcome: Match non-default executable Shell or Userinit values under Winlogon; do not match standard Explorer and Userinit values, unrelated keys or deletion events.
